theater: 河東平陽城與晉州城下

battle.name: 平陽之戰
battle.theater: 河東平陽城與晉州城下
battle.brief: 建德五年（五七六）十月至十二月，北周武帝宇文邕率軍東出，分兵扼守雀鼠谷、汾水關，內史王誼督主力攻平陽。十一月齊後主高緯親征逼城，周軍一度西撤；十二月再集兵約八萬於城下，大敗齊援軍，斬萬餘人，齊主敗退晉陽。卡面短劍非本戰實械，其直刺邏輯正對應北朝步卒的環首刀。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 平陽之戰是北周與北齊在河東的一次會戰。兩國同出北魏分裂，互為頭號敵手，正面對立已近三十年：東魏高歡於五三四年奠立，後由高洋代魏建齊；西魏宇文泰經營關隴，五五七年宇文覺代魏稱周。交戰於五百七十六年十月至十二月。北周的指揮體系以宇文泰奠基的關隴集團為核心，兵制以府兵為骨幹，配合宿衛、各州郡兵與鄉兵，軍政分由上開府、柱國、大將軍等高品武將掌握。周武帝宇文邕自五五七年即位後清除宇文護的專權，五七三年又禁佛寺、僧尼還俗、寺產入官，國庫為之一充，此役才能調集數萬大軍長驅轉用。十月出師時，宇文邕把兵權拆成左右三軍與前軍：越王宇文盛、杞公宇文亮、隋公楊堅為右三軍，譙王宇文儉、大將軍竇泰、廣化公丘崇為左三軍，齊王宇文憲、陳王宇文純為前軍，內史王誼總督攻平陽的主力，宇文憲等各將分領兵馬守禦雀鼠谷、千里徑、汾水關、統軍川等險隘。北齊方面以高緯為君，軍事大權分屬宿將段韶與幽州總管斛律光，沿用東魏的行台制度，州郡之上設行台尚書省，地方兵權與中央樞機交錯相糾。齊主把大量兵力與財貨集中於晉陽陪都，倚為北方根本，平陽、晉州一線由海昌王尉相貴、晉州刺史崔景嵩與行台左丞侯子欽分掌。齊軍以河東地區仍能供應的騎兵為骨幹，兼徵州郡步兵，徵發已難為繼，戰前可調集的野戰兵力明顯少於周軍。
countriesEn: The Battle of Pingyang was an engagement between Northern Zhou and Northern Qi in Hedong. Both states grew out of the split of Northern Wei and had been each other's foremost enemy for close to thirty years: Gao Huan established Eastern Wei in 534 and Gao Yang later replaced it with Qi, while Yuwen Tai built his power in Guanzhong and in 557 Yuwen Jue displaced Wei and proclaimed Northern Zhou. The action took place from October to December 576. On the Zhou side the command system rested on the Guanzhong group founded by Yuwen Tai, the backbone of the army being the fubing, supplemented by the palace guard, the departmental and commandery troops and the local militia, while military administration was divided among holders of high ranks such as the shang kaifu, the zhu guo and the da jiangjun. Emperor Wu of Zhou, Yuwen Yong, had taken the throne in 557 and destroyed the regency of Yuwen Hu; in 573 he suppressed the Buddhist temples, returned monks and nuns to lay life and confiscated temple estates into the treasury, and the state finances were still ample when this war was fought, which allowed tens of thousands of troops to be shifted a long distance. When he marched in October, Yuwen Yong split the command into a right, a left and a front group: Prince of Yue Yuwen Sheng, Duke of Qi Yuwen Liang and Duke of Sui Yang Jian commanded the right three armies, Prince of Qiao Yuwen Jian, General Dou Tai and Duke of Guanghua Qiu Chong the left three, while Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian and Prince of Chen Yuwen Chun led the vanguard. The Inner Secretary Wang Yi was given overall command of the main body assigned to attack Pingyang, and commanders such as Yuwen Xian took troops to hold the passes of Quelugu, Qianlijing, Fen Shuiguan and Tongjunchuan. On the Qi side the ruler was Gao Wei, and real military power was divided between the veteran Duan Shao and the commander of Youzhou, Hulü Guang. Qi retained the xingtai system of Eastern Wei, with an executive bureau set above the prefectures and commanderies, so that local and central military authority overlapped and complicated one another. Gao Wei concentrated troops and wealth at the secondary capital of Jinyang and treated it as the northern foundation of the state; the line of Pingyang and Jinzhou was held in parts by the Prince of Haichang Wei Xianggui, the governor of Jinzhou Cui Jingsong and the left deputy of the xingtai Hou Ziqin. The Qi army was built on the cavalry that the Hedong region could still supply, mixed with infantry levied from the prefectures and commanderies; such levies were no longer easy to sustain, and the field force it could bring to the battle was clearly smaller than that of Zhou.
people: 北周一方，主帥是周武帝宇文邕。他曾於五百七十五年第一次北伐，因病班師，隔年再發：先駐汾曲、進逼晉州，又在齊主親征、來軍氣盛時主動西撤以避其鋒，把主力撤出晉州，只留兵一萬交梁士彥固守平陽，待援軍與戰局回轉再親自回師——此役多數關鍵決策都集中在他一人之手。宇文憲是此役最吃重的將領，他為宇文泰之子、周武帝之弟，先領兵二萬守雀鼠谷，截斷齊軍自晉陽南下的通道；西撤之戰中，他與宇文忻任後衛，斬齊將賀蘭豹子等，迫使齊師退回；其後又率六萬屯涑川，為平陽的守軍與援軍作策應。內史王誼是攻平陽的實際前線統帥，率主力圍城。上開府儀同大將軍王軌在關鍵時刻受降晉州刺史崔景嵩，遣部將段文振為先遣率先登城，內應得手，平陽、晉州一帶的城邑因之迅速易手。越王宇文盛、杞公宇文亮、隋公楊堅、譙王宇文儉、大將軍竇泰、廣化公丘崇、陳王宇文純分領各路兵馬，扼守雀鼠谷、千里徑、汾水關、統軍川、齊子嶺、鼓鐘鎮、蒲津關與華谷，把齊軍可能的援兵線一條條掐斷；隋公楊堅即其後代周建隋的那位楊堅，此時已在北周高層將領之列。北齊一方，齊後主高緯居中樞而不能制軍，宿將段韶與幽州總管斛律光在北方握有實兵，但高緯臨陣親征而謀乏良斷。十一月他御駕親征平陽，正是出於馮小憐之請；齊軍挖掘地道、攻塌城牆十餘步、乘勢即可入城之際，馮淑妃卻認為齊兵大破周兵的場面壯觀，應先梳妝打扮，高緯遂下令收兵觀看，一舉失掉破城的良機。平陽守將尉相貴被俘，晉州刺史崔景嵩與行台左丞侯子欽相繼出降，齊軍的士氣與指揮體系自此崩解；而留守平陽的梁士彥在周軍退去後獨力固守，晝夜抵禦齊軍攻擊，以一當百，擊退齊師。
peopleEn: On the Zhou side the commander-in-chief was Emperor Wu of Zhou, Yuwen Yong. He had marched against Qi in 575 and withdrawn because of illness, and he returned the following year: he first took up position at Fenqu and pressed towards Jinzhou, and when the Qi ruler came up in person with an army that outnumbered his own, he deliberately withdrew west to avoid the Qi advance, pulling the main body out of Jinzhou and leaving only ten thousand men under Liang Shiyan to hold Pingyang, waiting until the situation turned before returning in person. Most of the decisive judgements in this campaign were his alone. Yuwen Xian was the most heavily burdened commander of the Zhou force, a son of Yuwen Tai and brother of the emperor; he first took twenty thousand men to hold Quelugu and cut the road by which Qi troops would come south from Jinyang, and in the fighting during the withdrawal he and Yuwen Xin served as rearguard, killing the Qi commander Helan Baozi and others, which turned the Qi army back. Later he took sixty thousand men to camp on the Sui river, screening the garrison at Pingyang and the relieving army. The Inner Secretary Wang Yi was the actual front-line commander of the siege of Pingyang, directing the main body. The Shang kaifu and Tong da jiangjun Wang Ji met the submission of the governor of Jinzhou, Cui Jingsong, at the critical moment and sent his subordinate Duan Wenzhen ahead as the first party onto the wall; the breach being opened from within, the towns of Pingyang and Jinzhou changed hands quickly. Prince of Yue Yuwen Sheng, Duke of Qi Yuwen Liang, Duke of Sui Yang Jian, Prince of Qiao Yuwen Jian, General Dou Tai, Duke of Guanghua Qiu Chong and Prince of Chen Yuwen Chun led separate columns which held Quelugu, Qianlijing, Fen Shuiguan, Tongjunchuan, Qiziling, Gulongzhen, Pujin Pass and Huagu, cutting off one by one the lines along which Qi reinforcements might come. Duke of Sui Yang Jian was the very Yang Jian who would later replace Zhou and found the Sui dynasty, and he already stood among the senior commanders of Northern Zhou. On the Qi side the ruler was the last emperor of Qi, Gao Wei, who sat at the centre of power without being able to direct the army. The veteran Duan Shao and the Youzhou commander Hulü Guang held real troops in the north, yet Gao Wei came out in person without the judgement the moment required. In November he rode to Pingyang in person precisely at the request of Feng Xiaolian. When the Qi miners had tunnelled under the wall, brought down more than ten paces of it and were on the point of entering the city, Feng Shufei declared that the sight of the Qi army defeating the Zhou was magnificent and ought to be watched after she had made herself ready; Gao Wei accordingly ordered the army to stand down and watch, throwing away the moment when the city could have been taken. Wei Xianggui, the defender of Pingyang, was captured; Cui Jingsong and Hou Ziqin surrendered in turn, and from then on the morale and command structure of the Qi army fell apart. Liang Shiyan, who was left to hold Pingyang, defended it alone after the Zhou army withdrew, meeting the Qi attacks day and night and beating them off in spite of the odds.
kits: 卡面上的羅馬短劍是共和末期至帝國早期羅馬步兵的標準冷兵器：雙刃、護手寬闊、重心靠前，設計上只為直刺而存在，須配合大盾的邊緣與出刺的節奏使用，並與投槍、長矛組成步戰組合。它並不可能出現在五百七十六年的河東戰場；就功能而言，這一役真正與之對應的，是北朝步卒手中的環首刀——單手直刃、刀身素面、刀環以帶鍊相連，便於在短兵相接時連刺帶格，而騎兵所用則是長杆的槊與較沉的環首刀。雙方步兵的骨幹仍是矛，長矛成排用以迎拒騎兵衝鋒；鎲（錘）用於砸破盾面與打擊甲胄縫隙。防護上，北朝步兵持木胎漆面的小盾遮蔽身體與面臨來自側翼的箭矢，兜鍪與札甲、明光一類的圓領護肩甲同時配置，北方墓葬出土的北朝陶盔與鐵甲片可以印證這類裝備的形制。騎兵方面，馬鎧與騎士具裝在北朝已不罕見，斛律光所部精騎是齊軍最具壓迫力的打擊力量。弓箭方面，角弓、膠弓與反曲弓在兩軍之中都廣為配置，步騎皆能施放。攻城與守城的器物在這一役留下了具體痕跡：齊軍挖掘地道以攻塌牆身，周軍則砍木塞住被挖穿的缺口，使其不能擴大；守城一方還備有雲梯、撞車一類常見器械與以膏油附矢的火攻之物。至於卡面短劍所提示的那個道理——近身交鋒靠刺而非砍、靠節奏而非蠻力——在北朝步卒以刀矛結成的密集陣線裡同樣成立，只是那時的節奏由鼓點、旗幟與號角給出，而不由盾緣給出。
kitsEn: The Roman gladius on the card was the standard cold weapon of Roman infantry from the late Republic into the early Empire: double-edged, with a broad guard and the centre of gravity carried forward, it was designed purely for the thrust and had to be used with the edge of the large shield and the rhythm of the blow, paired with the pilum and the long spear to form the infantry's kit. It could never have appeared on a battlefield in Hedong in 576; the true counterpart in function in this campaign is the huanshou dao of the Northern dynasties, a single-handed straight blade with a plain tang and a ring at the pommel, suited to stabbing and hooking in close fighting, while the cavalry carried the long-shafted shuo and the heavier ring-pommel sword. The backbone of infantry on both sides remained the spear, ranks of long spears being turned against charging horse; the mace was used to break shields and to strike through the gaps of armour. For protection the Northern infantry carried small shields of lacquered wood to cover the body and the arrows arriving from the flank, while helmets and lamellar or Mingguang-type cuirasses with round collars and shoulder defences were worn as well, and Northern dynasty pottery helmets and iron armour plates excavated from tombs in the north confirm the form of this equipment. On the cavalry side, caparisoned horses and fully armoured riders were no longer rare in the Northern dynasties, and the picked cavalry under Hulü Guang was the most oppressive striking force of the Qi army. Bows of horn and composite recurve types were carried on both sides, by foot and mounted alike. The siege and defence equipment left clear traces in this campaign: the Qi miners drove a tunnel under the wall, and the Zhou cut timber to plug the opening so that it could not be widened; the defenders also had the usual ladders, battering rams and fire-arrow preparations with oil and grease. As for the principle the gladius on the card stands for — that close fighting is decided by the thrust rather than the cut, and by rhythm rather than brute strength — it held just as truly in the close-packed ranks of Northern infantry armed with dao and spear. Only the tempo there was given by drums, banners and horns, and not by the edge of a shield.
tactics: 此役的戰術骨架是一張由隘口組成的網。十月上中旬，周軍抵汾曲、晉州，宇文盛、宇文純、達奚震分別以步兵、步騎兵一萬至兩萬守汾水關、千里徑、統軍川，辛韶五千守蒲津關，韓明五千守齊子嶺，尹升五千赴鼓鐘鎮，宇文招率步騎兵一萬自華谷出擊汾水以西諸城，宇文憲領二萬守雀鼠谷，意圖同時掐斷晉陽齊軍南下與河內齊軍北上的兩條路，並封住左翼與後方。主力由內史王誼率領直取平陽城。攻城不靠強攻而靠內應：晉州刺史崔景嵩見無後援而請降，王軌遣段文振率數十人為先遣率先登城，內應成功，尉相貴與士卒八千人被俘，平陽、晉州一線失守。十一月齊後主親征而來，周軍避其兵盛，撤出晉州只留一萬兵守平陽，齊軍追擊西撤之師，宇文憲、宇文忻任後衛反擊斬賀蘭豹子等，齊師乃退，改用地道攻城，牆塌十餘步，幾乎入城，卻因馮淑妃主張梳妝觀戰而收兵，周軍得以砍木塞城，缺口不得擴大。接著周武帝令宇文憲率六萬屯涑川作策應，留諸軍於河東，親自還長安；齊軍晝夜圍攻平陽，梁士彥以一當百多方固守，把齊師擊退。十二月宇文邕再率援軍返回，於城下集兵約八萬，近城列陣，東西二十餘里，奮擊大破齊援軍，斬萬餘人，齊主敗退晉陽，周軍乘勝進軍晉陽。整體看，周軍靠分割隘口、內應取城、木塞堵缺三步穩住戰線，最後以會戰兵力一決勝負；齊軍則兩次失分，一在破城之際收兵觀看，二在援軍尚未集結即被城下主力擊潰。
tacticsEn: The tactical skeleton of this campaign was a net of passes. In the middle of October the Zhou army reached Fenqu and Jinzhou; Yuwen Sheng, Yuwen Chun and Daxi Zhen took infantry or mixed infantry and cavalry of ten to twenty thousand men to Fen Shuiguan, Qianlijing and Tongjunchuan, Xin Shao five thousand to Pujin Pass, Han Ming five thousand to Qiziling, Yin Sheng five thousand to Gulongzhen, and Yuwen Zhao ten thousand mixed troops to strike the towns west of the Fen river from Huagu, while Yuwen Xian held Quelugu with twenty thousand, the intention being to cut at once both the road by which the Qi army of Jinyang would march south and the road by which the Qi forces of Henei would march north, while sealing the left flank and the rear. The main body under the Inner Secretary Wang Yi was to take Pingyang outright. The city was not stormed but opened: the governor of Jinzhou, Cui Jingsong, seeing that no help was coming, offered to surrender, and Wang Ji sent his subordinate Duan Wenzhen ahead with a few dozen men to mount the wall first; the entry from within succeeded, Wei Xianggui and eight thousand of his men were taken, and the line of Pingyang and Jinzhou was lost. In November the Qi ruler came in person and advanced with a numerous army; the Zhou withdrew from Jinzhou to avoid the stronger force, leaving ten thousand men to hold Pingyang, and the Qi pursued the withdrawing army, but Yuwen Xian and Yuwen Xin turned as rearguard, killed Helan Baozi and others, and the Qi fell back, turning instead to a mine under the wall. More than ten paces of the wall came down and they were on the point of entering, but Feng Shufei wanted to dress herself before watching so magnificent a sight, the army was stood down, and the Zhou cut timber to plug the breach so that it could not widen. Yuwen Yong then ordered Yuwen Xian to hold sixty thousand men on the Sui river as a second line, left the rest of the army in Hedong, and returned himself to Chang'an; the Qi surrounded Pingyang and attacked day and night, and Liang Shiyan, fighting as one against many, held the city by every means and beat the Qi off. In December Yuwen Yong came back with reinforcements, concentrated about eighty thousand men below the city, drew them up close to the walls over a front of more than twenty li from east to west, and by a furious charge routed the Qi relief army, cutting down more than ten thousand men; the Qi ruler fell back on Jinyang and the Zhou army pressed on after him. In sum, the Zhou stabilised the line by dividing the enemy with the passes, taking towns by submission from within and plugging the breach with timber, and finally decided the issue in a pitched battle; the Qi lost ground twice, first by standing down to watch while the city was about to fall, and second because their relief army was beaten before it had gathered.
data: 可核對的數字以《資治通鑑》卷一百七十二所記最為具體。分路兵力：宇文憲守雀鼠谷二萬，宇文純守千里徑步騎兵二萬，宇文盛守汾水關步兵一萬，達奚震守統軍川步騎兵一萬，韓明守齊子嶺步騎兵五千，尹升赴鼓鐘鎮步騎兵五千，辛韶扼蒲津關步騎兵五千，宇文招自華谷出擊步騎兵一萬，涑川策應兵力六萬。各路相加已近八萬，加上王誼所督主力與十二月集於平陽城下的約八萬，兩組數字顯然不是同一支兵力的兩次清點，而是分段記帳，說明史書的兵額多屬概略之辭。斬獲方面：平陽、晉州易手時俘尉相貴及士卒八千人；十二月城下會戰斬萬餘人。戰陣寬度記為東西二十餘里，即前鋒展開約十公里上下。距離方面，蒲津關在今永濟西，與平陽之間沿汾水逆流而上約三四百里，是周軍後方與關中聯絡的命脈；平陽至齊軍根本晉陽約二百餘里；雀鼠谷、千里徑、汾水關、統軍川同處汾水峽谷通道，彼此相距不遠而地勢險要，故能以少量兵力封鎖數百里的出入；涑川距平陽僅數十里，是策應的支點。時間上，十月出師、十一月齊主親征與地道攻城、十二月城下會戰，全役歷時約兩個月，正趕上汾水流域秋冬霜降、晝夜溫差極大之際。地道造成的缺口記為十餘步，按當時一步約合一點五米計，約合二十米上下，數目雖小，卻足以讓攻方在城頭失去縱深。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are given most concretely in the first hundred and seventy-second chapter of the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance. The strength of each column: Yuwen Xian held Quelugu with twenty thousand, Yuwen Chun held Qianlijing with twenty thousand of infantry and cavalry, Yuwen Sheng held Fen Shuiguan with ten thousand infantry, Daxi Zhen held Tongjunchuan with ten thousand mixed troops, Han Ming held Qiziling with five thousand mixed troops, Yin Sheng was sent to Gulongzhen with five thousand, Xin Shao held Pujin Pass with five thousand, Yuwen Zhao struck out from Huagu with ten thousand mixed troops, and sixty thousand were camped on the Sui river as a second line. These add up to nearly eighty thousand, and with the main body under Wang Yi and the eighty thousand reported at Pingyang in December the two groups plainly are not two enumerations of the same force but separate book-keeping, which shows that the troop numbers in the chronicles are rough estimates. As for results: when Pingyang and Jinzhou changed hands, Wei Xianggui and eight thousand of his men were taken prisoner; in the battle below the city in December more than ten thousand of the Qi were killed. The breadth of the deployed line is given as more than twenty li from east to west, that is a front of roughly ten kilometres. As for distances: Pujin Pass lay west of the modern Yongji, and from there up the Fen river to Pingyang was some three to four hundred li, the artery by which the Zhou rear areas stayed in touch with Guanzhong; from Pingyang to Jinyang, the Qi base, was about two hundred and some li; and Quelugu, Qianlijing, Fen Shuiguan and Tongjunchuan all lay along the gorge road of the Fen river, not far from one another but commanding difficult ground, so that small bodies could close off a stretch of several hundred li. The Sui river was only some tens of li from Pingyang and served as the pivot of the supporting force. In time, the army marched in October, the Qi ruler came in person and the mining of the wall took place in November, and the battle below the city was fought in December, so that the whole campaign lasted about two months, in the middle of the frost and the sharp day-night temperature swings of autumn and winter in the Fen valley. The breach made by the mine is given as more than ten paces, which at roughly one and a half metres to the pace amounts to about twenty metres; small in itself, but enough to strip the defenders of depth along the wall.
cause: 打起來的原因，一半在北齊的積弊，一半在北周的準備。北齊末年，齊主高緯把大量人力財貨投入晉陽陪都的營建與封賞，州郡的徵發與租調日益窘迫，軍隊戰意低落，宿將段韶與斛律光各有重兵，朝廷卻屢屢更換統帥、猜忌功臣，齊軍的野戰兵員在開戰前已經難以為繼。齊主把晉陽視為北方根本，平陽與晉州便是通往河東腹地的門戶，一旦失守，齊軍便再無縱深可退。北周方面，宇文邕自五五七年親政後清除宇文護的權柄，五七三年禁絕佛寺、僧尼還俗、寺產入官，使國庫充盈，府兵與州郡兵的徵發也更為整齊；對外則與北面的突厥和親結盟，趙王宇文聘尚突厥俟斤之女，解除側翼威脅，使北周可以專力東向。五七五年第一次北伐已因宇文邕生病而中斷，說明這條攻勢早已醞釀成熟，隔年再發只是把時機補上。戰前周軍還刻意在多處製造可以內應的裂口，崔景嵩與侯子欽先後出降，正是齊方內部虛耗、人心不附的徵候。十月的出師，實質是以兵力和時間去撬開齊國北翼的門樞。
causeEn: The reasons for the fighting lie half in the accumulated failings of Northern Qi and half in the preparations of Northern Zhou. In the last years of Qi, the ruler Gao Wei poured labour and wealth into the building and rewarding of the secondary capital at Jinyang, levies and taxes on the prefectures and commanderies grew ever more strained, and the army's will to fight sagged; the veterans Duan Shao and Hulü Guang each held substantial troops, yet the court repeatedly changed commanders and distrusted its own meritorious generals, so that the Qi field force was already hard to sustain before the war began. The Qi ruler treated Jinyang as the northern foundation of the state, and Pingyang and Jinzhou were the gateways into the belly of Hedong; once they were lost, the Qi army would have no depth left to fall back on. On the Zhou side, Yuwen Yong had taken personal control after 557 and destroyed the power of Yuwen Hu; in 573 he suppressed the Buddhist temples, returned monks and nuns to lay life and brought temple estates into the treasury, which filled the treasury and made the levies of the fubing and of the departmental troops more orderly; abroad he sealed an alliance with the Turks to the north by marrying the Prince of Zhao Yuwen Pin to a daughter of the Turkic chieftain, removing the threat on his flank so that Zhou could concentrate on the east. The northern campaign of 575 had already been broken off because Yuwen Yong fell ill, which shows that this line of attack was long prepared and that the following year only supplied the missing moment. Before the campaign the Zhou army deliberately opened seams in which submission from within was possible, and the surrenders of Cui Jingsong and Hou Ziqin were themselves symptoms of the exhaustion and the loss of confidence on the Qi side. The march of October was in substance an attempt to prise open the hinge of Qi's northern defence with troops and with time.
impact: 平陽的失守與十二月的慘敗，改變了北齊的戰爭形態。齊軍在河東的西翼被切斷，齊主只能退保晉陽，把野戰兵力收縮為守城之資，北齊由主動轉為純防禦；然而齊國並未就此覆亡，段韶等宿將仍在，晉陽的城防也確實堅固，因此這場戰爭的直接後果，是把北齊又延續了約一年。對北周而言，平陽之役同時是一次代價不小的攻城教材：齊軍的地道幾乎成功，靠砍木塞城才被擋住，而齊軍反過來晝夜圍攻平陽，又被梁士彥擊退，說明六世紀北方軍隊的攻城技術仍處在摸索階段，爆破的可行性已現，配套的封堵手段卻不成熟；一年之後北周改採輕兵疾進、直取鄴城而不與齊軍逐城爭奪，方向上的修正正源於此。政事上，平陽之戰暴露了齊主高緯的昏聵，馮淑妃兩度介入軍務而誤事，朝廷對宿將的猜忌隨之加深，一年後斛律光及其子斛律羨相繼被誅與戰歿，齊軍人心崩潰，滅齊之役遂成定局。長遠看，五百七十六年的這一仗是北周統一北方的起手，五百七十七年北齊覆亡，五百七十八年周武帝病逝、宣帝宇文贇荒淫、楊堅專權，最終五百八十一年隋代周，北方由分裂再度歸於一統，平陽之役正是這條鏈條上最早、最具體的一環。
impactEn: The loss of Pingyang and the crushing defeat in December changed the shape of the Qi war. The Qi western flank in Hedong was cut, the Qi ruler could only fall back on Jinyang and contract his field army into a garrison, and Northern Qi passed from the offensive to pure defence; yet the state did not collapse at once, since veterans such as Duan Shao were still in the field and the defences of Jinyang were genuinely strong, so the direct consequence of this war was to extend Northern Qi by roughly another year. For Zhou, Pingyang was at the same time a costly lesson in siege work: the Qi mine had almost succeeded and was only stopped by timber plugged into the breach, while the Qi in turn surrounded Pingyang day and night and were beaten off by Liang Shiyan, which shows that siegecraft in the northern armies of the sixth century was still experimental — the feasibility of mining had appeared, but the means of sealing a breach were not yet developed. A year later Zhou changed its approach, moving fast with a light force straight at Ye instead of contesting town after town with the Qi, and that correction of direction grew directly out of what had been learned here. In politics, the battle exposed the folly of the Qi ruler Gao Wei: Feng Shufei twice intervened in military business and ruined the business both times, and the court's suspicion of its veteran commanders deepened. A year later Hulü Guang was put to death and his son Hulü Xian was killed in action, the Qi army's morale collapsed, and the destruction of Qi became a settled thing. In the long run the campaign of 576 was the opening move in the reunification of the north under Zhou; Qi fell in 577, Wu of Zhou died in 578, his successor Yuwen Yun was dissolute, Yang Jian took power, and in 581 the Sui replaced the Zhou, so that the north passed once more from division to unity. The Battle of Pingyang is the earliest and most concrete link in that chain.
result: 就戰果而言，平陽之役是一場界於大勝與未竟之間的戰爭。周軍以內應取下平陽、晉州，俘尉相貴及士卒八千人，切斷了齊軍在河東的西翼；十二月再以約八萬人列陣城下，東西二十餘里，奮擊大破齊援軍，斬萬餘人，齊主高緯敗退晉陽，北齊一時喪失平原與河東的縱深。但此役終未消滅北齊：周軍未能攻下晉陽，齊軍在段韶等宿將之手與堅固城防之下守住了北方根本，北周大軍因糧道綿長、秋冬行軍與攻城消耗而不得不班師，平陽等城邑隨即重回齊軍控制之下，齊國又勉強維持了近一年。平陽的真正意義在於條件的改變：齊國西翼已失，野戰主力一戰而盡，只能退守晉陽與鄴城；而北周也由此摸清了北方的地形與城防，翌年改為集中兵力直取鄴城，齊軍未及成列而潰，鄴城陷落，幽州刺史馮小瑀率眾而降，北齊遂亡。換言之，這一仗並未終結戰爭，卻把戰爭的結束方式與時間表都定下來了：從平陽到晉陽，再到鄴城，北周的兩步取齊路線，源於此役的勝負與教訓，而真正決定平陽城下勝負的並不是卡面短劍所代表的近身短兵，而是隘口的分割、內應的奇襲、冬季作戰的耐力與會戰兵力的集結。
resultEn: As for the military result, Pingyang was a victory that fell short of ending the war. The Zhou army took Pingyang and Jinzhou by submission from within, capturing Wei Xianggui and eight thousand men and cutting the Qi western flank in Hedong; in December it deployed about eighty thousand men below the city over a front of more than twenty li from east to west and by a furious charge routed the Qi relief army, cutting down more than ten thousand men, and the Qi ruler Gao Wei fell back on Jinyang, so that Northern Qi for a time lost the depths of the plain and of Hedong. Yet the war was not ended there: the Zhou did not take Jinyang, the Qi held its northern foundation under veterans such as Duan Shao and behind strong defences, and the long Zhou columns, exhausted by the length of their supply line and by campaigning and sieging in the cold of autumn and winter, had to withdraw, after which places such as Pingyang came back under Qi control and the state limped on for close to another year. The real meaning of Pingyang lay in how it changed the conditions: the Qi had lost its western flank and its field army was destroyed in a single battle, so it could only fall back on Jinyang and Ye; and the Zhou had learned the northern terrain and the northern fortifications, so that the following year it concentrated its forces to strike straight at Ye, where the Qi army broke before it could be drawn up and the city fell, the governor of Youzhou, Feng Xiaoyu, came over with his men, and Northern Qi ceased to exist. In other words, this battle did not end the war, but it settled both the way and the timetable of the ending: from Pingyang to Jinyang and then to Ye, the two-step road by which Zhou destroyed Qi grew out of the outcome and the lessons of this engagement. What actually decided the fight below Pingyang was not the short sword represented by the card, but the partition of the enemy by passes, the surprise worked through the submission from within, the endurance of winter campaigning and the concentration of strength for the decisive battle.
